transit.name: Black Hawk Shuttle
transit.detail: Free, ADA-accessible shuttle running seven days a week along Main Street and Gregory Street, with 16 stops.

nameOrigin.text: The Gilpin Historical Society says the town, first called Black Hawk Point, took its name from the Rock Island, Illinois foundry that made one of the earliest stamp mills brought into the district.

founded.text: William L. Lee, Dr. Frederick H. Judd and Mylo Lee founded the town of Black Hawk Point in June 1860.

timeline.text: Prospector John H. Gregory found lode gold in the ravine that became known as Gregory Gulch.
Black Hawk was incorporated on March 11 as the second incorporated city in the Colorado Territory.
The railroad arrived and linked Black Hawk to Denver.
The first casinos opened in historic Black Hawk buildings.

sites.name: Historic Gilpin Tramway Trail (Maryland Mountain Quartz Valley Open Space Park)

trails.name: Golden Gate Canyon State Park
trails.size: 12,119 acres with 35 miles of trails, 156 campsites and 125 picnic sites
trails.address: 92 Crawford Gulch Road, Golden, CO 80403; the visitor center is at Golden Gate Canyon Road (Highway 46) and Crawford Gulch Road
trails.season: Day use 5 am to 10 pm. Mountain Base Road is closed for the winter from November 1; reach the upper park by Highway 46 and Highway 119 to Gap Road. Visitor center Tuesday to Sunday, 9 am to 4 pm.
trails.fee: Daily vehicle pass $10 to $12 with a Colorado plate, $15 to $17 out of state (the page’s summary box says $12 to $17); $4 on foot, bike or horse; $80 annual pass. Nine self-pay kiosks in the park.
